title: Scalar-compatible rational derived pullback fibre comparison
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be its base change to $k$, and put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Choose geometric points $\bar z:s\to X$, $\bar x:s\to Y$ with $f\bar z=\bar x$. Use the framework rationalized categories and their common-stage categories [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and point fibres [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For a finite coefficient field $E\subset\Qlb$, put $J_{z,E}=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}L\bar z_E^*$ and $J_{x,E}=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}L\bar x_E^*$. Use the specified composition and scalar comparisons of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] and the point-sections comparisons of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension].

There is a natural isomorphism of functors to $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$,
$$c^E_M:J_{z,E}Lf_E^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{x,E}M,$$
whose component is $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$ of the inverse of $L(f\bar z)_E^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}L\bar z_E^*Lf_E^*M$. For $E\subset L$, write $T_U=-\otimes_E L$ on $U=X,Y$, $a_{f,M}:T_XLf_E^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf_L^*T_YM$ for the specified scalar comparison, and $b_{z,N}:J_{z,E}N\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{z,L}T_XN$, $b_{x,M}:J_{x,E}M\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{x,L}T_YM$ for the specified fibre scalar comparisons. Then
$$c^L_{T_YM}\,J_{z,L}(a_{f,M})\,b_{z,Lf_E^*M}=b_{x,M}(c^E_M\otimes_E L).$$
These comparisons respect identity coefficient extensions and the specified associators for $E\subset L\subset H$. They therefore induce a natural $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism $c:J_zLf^*\xrightarrow{\sim}J_x$ in the derived category of common-stage point complexes, independent of representatives. The assertion applies to all constructible complexes; no Weil structure, integral Weil-stable lattice, or finite Tor-amplitude of finite reductions is required.

proof.text: Write $P_{g,E}=Lg_E^*$ and $V_E=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$. The specified comparison of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], rationalized as in its statement, gives $d_E:P_{\bar x,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{\bar z,E}P_{f,E}$, since $f\bar z=\bar x$. Define $c^E=V_E(d_E^{-1})$. The pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the fibre functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] have the required constructible and finite-dimensional derived targets. Naturality of $d_E$ and functoriality of $V_E$ show, for $u:M\to N$, that $c^E_NJ_{z,E}P_{f,E}(u)=J_{x,E}(u)c^E_M$. Its inverse is $V_E(d_E)$, so this is the required natural isomorphism, with exactly the specified component.

proof.text:
Let $T_s$ denote coefficient extension at $s$. For a scheme map $g$ use $a_g:T P_{g,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{g,L}T$ from [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Write $\beta_K:V_E(K)\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}V_L(T_sK)$ for the inverse of the rational sections comparison in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. The specified fibre comparison is $b_{z,N}=V_L(a_{\bar z,N})\beta_{P_{\bar z,E}N}$, and similarly for $x$. Specializing the mixed equation of the first cited node to $h=\bar z$, $k=f$ gives
$$P_{\bar z,L}(a_{f,M})a_{\bar z,P_{f,E}M}T_s(d_{E,M})=d_{L,T_YM}a_{\bar x,M}.$$
Multiplying on the left by $d_{L,T_YM}^{-1}$ and on the right by $T_s(d_{E,M}^{-1})$ yields
$$d_{L,T_YM}^{-1}P_{\bar z,L}(a_{f,M})a_{\bar z,P_{f,E}M}=a_{\bar x,M}T_s(d_{E,M}^{-1}).$$
This uses equality of the scheme maps $f\bar z$ and $\bar x$, which that cited comparison explicitly respects.

proof.text:
Apply $V_L$ to the last equality and precompose with $\beta_{P_{\bar z,E}P_{f,E}M}$. Naturality of the rational sections comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] gives
$$V_L(T_s(d_{E,M}^{-1}))\beta_{P_{\bar z,E}P_{f,E}M}=\beta_{P_{\bar x,E}M}(V_E(d_{E,M}^{-1})\otimes_E L).$$
Inserting the definitions of $b_z,b_x,c^E,c^L$ from the preceding steps therefore gives exactly
$$c^L_{T_YM}J_{z,L}(a_{f,M})b_{z,P_{f,E}M}=b_{x,M}(c^E_M\otimes_E L).$$
These equations are equations of morphisms of derived objects, before taking any cohomology.

proof.text: For an identity extension $E= L$, both $a_g$ and $\beta$ are identities under the specified unit identifications, by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] and [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. For $E\subset L\subset H$, those same statements give the tower equations for $a_g$ and $\beta$ with the specified tensor associators. Substituting $b_z=V(a_{\bar z})\beta$ into its twice-extended expression, naturality of $\beta$ moves the inner $a_{\bar z}$ past the outer $\beta$. The two adjacent $a_{\bar z}$ maps become the direct $E\subset H$ map by the first tower equation; the two remaining $\beta$ maps become its direct sections map by the second. Thus $b_z$, and identically $b_x$, have the required tower law. The mixed equation in Step 2 also respects these associators by the first cited statement, so the square of Step 3 for the two successive extensions is the square for $E\subset H$.

proof.text: Use the common-stage representatives of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the functors of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Put $F_E=J_{z,E}P_{f,E}$, $G_E=J_{x,E}$, $A_M=J_{z,L}(a_{f,M})b_{z,P_{f,E}M}$ and $B_M=b_{x,M}$. Step 3 says $c^L_{T_YM}A_M=B_M(c^E_M\otimes_E L)$. Hence the class of $c^E_M$ is the same component after changing stage, and so is the class of its inverse. For a morphism represented over $L$ by $u:T M\to T N$ (allowing different original fields), the two functors act by $A_N^{-1}F_L(u)A_M$ and $B_N^{-1}G_L(u)B_M$. Using the displayed square at both ends, the desired naturality equation reduces to $c^L_{TN}F_L(u)=G_L(u)c^L_{TM}$, proved in Step 1. Equal representatives become equal over a further common field by the cited common-stage definition; Step 4 makes their conjugated maps and these equations equal there too. This proves independence, naturality and invertibility in the common-stage derived category. At every finite stage all operations are linear; representing a scalar in $\Qlb$ in a common finite extension therefore proves $\Qlb$-linearity. The composition comparison cited in Step 1 expressly imposes no finite Tor-amplitude condition, and all its inputs are arbitrary constructible complexes. No Weil datum or Weil-stable lattice entered any step.
